name: Travel Checklist
description: An end-to-end travel checklist for planning a trip, from booking and documents to money, health, home prep, and packing.

items.text: Set your dates, destination, and rough budget
Book flights, trains, or other transport
Reserve accommodation for each night
Arrange airport transfers or a rental car
Book key tours, tickets, and activities
items.note: Popular activities sell out, so book early

items.text: Build a simple day-by-day itinerary
Check passport and ID validity for the trip
Confirm any visa or entry requirements
Print or save all booking confirmations
Make copies of key documents, kept separately
Save digital copies in the cloud and on your phone
Notify your bank of your travel dates
Arrange local currency or a travel card
Set a daily budget and track expenses
Check phone roaming, eSIM, or local SIM options
Download maps and key apps for offline use
Arrange travel insurance with medical coverage
Check vaccine and health requirements early
Pack medicines and copies of prescriptions
Note clinics and the local emergency number
Confirm requirements via official government sources
items.note: Health and entry rules vary by country, so verify with official sources

items.text: Pause mail, newspapers, and deliveries
Arrange care for pets and plants
Secure doors, windows, and valuables
Unplug non-essential electronics
Set lights on a timer or ask a neighbor to check in
Empty the fridge of items that will spoil
Pack clothes, toiletries, and tech using a packing list
Keep documents, money, and medicines in your carry-on
Charge devices and pack chargers and adapters
Weigh bags against airline limits
Confirm departure times and check in online
Do a final sweep for keys, wallet, and phone

faq.q: When should I start using a travel checklist?
faq.a: Start four to six weeks before departure for most trips, and earlier for international travel that needs visas or vaccines. Early planning gives you time to compare prices, sort documents, and avoid last-minute fees.

faq.q: What is the difference between a travel checklist and a packing checklist?
faq.a: A travel checklist covers the whole trip — bookings, documents, money, health, and home prep — while a packing checklist focuses only on what goes in your bags. Use this list to plan and a packing list to fill your luggage.

faq.q: How do I prepare my home before traveling?
faq.a: Pause mail and deliveries, secure doors and windows, unplug non-essential electronics, set timers or ask a neighbor to check in, and arrange care for pets and plants. A tidy, secure home is easier to return to.

Travel insurance is worth considering, especially for international trips, big bookings, or anything non-refundable. Compare coverage for medical care, cancellations, and lost baggage, and read the policy details before buying.
Yes. Print it or download the PDF, start a few weeks before your trip, and check off each item as you book, prepare, and pack your way to departure.
